prompt:
I need the front end for Codewalk. A subscription reference tool for independent permit expediters and small design professionals that brings the zoning and building codes of several municipalities into one place they can move through, with their client projects attached.

Who's using it: Rosa Delgado, a self-employed permit expediter in the East Bay with 14 years of experience. She files residential permits for homeowners and small builders in three cities and works alone from a home office.

What they're doing right now: A client wants to build a 720 sq ft detached ADU in the rear yard of a corner lot in Alameda's R-2 district. Rosa has to confirm the rear and street-side setbacks, whether the state ADU law overrides the local height limit, and which permit pathway applies. She started in Alameda's zoning chapter, followed a cross-reference into the ADU section, then into the state Government Code. Now she needs to find her way back to the R-2 table, compare it with the corner-lot exceptions in another chapter, and check how Oakland treats the same issue, since a second client there has a near-identical lot. She needs to keep track of where she has been and which sections she has saved to each client file.

What's in the system at this point: 3 jurisdictions: City of Alameda Municipal Code (Title 30 Development Regulations, 412 sections), City of Oakland Planning Code (Title 17, 690 sections), and California Government Code §§66314–66342 (ADU law). Each section has a number, title, last amendment date (e.g. 'AMC 30-5.18, amended Ord. 3341, Mar 2025'), and cross-references to other sections. 11 active client files, e.g. '1418 Pacific Ave – Kwan ADU' and '3307 Brookdale – Ferreira ADU', each with 2–9 saved sections and Rosa's notes. Recently visited: 17 sections this session. Permit types per city with stage names (Intake, Plan Check, Corrections, Issued).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
